chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Masud, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal, from al-Abbas ibn Amir and Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira al-Nasri who said:

I heard Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan asking Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he did not cease asking him until he said to him: 'So the people were destroyed?' He said: 'Yes, by Allah, O son of A'yan, all the people were destroyed.' I said: 'Whoever was in the East and whoever was in the West?' He said: 'Indeed, it was opened up to misguidance, yes, by Allah, they were all destroyed except three, then Abu Sasan, Ammar, Shatira and Abu Umra joined them, so they became seven.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the seven people who were not destroyed according to the hadith of Rijal al-Kashshi?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal*, Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan questions Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the state of the Muslim community after the Prophet, to which the Imam confirms that the masses perished in misguidance, leaving only a select few. While initially only three remained, the number expanded to seven as Abu Sasan, Ammar, Shatira, and Abu Umra joined the righteous remnant, highlighting the concept of *al-Najiyun* (the saved few) in early Shia eschatology. This narration underscores the scholarly tradition of identifying specific companions as carriers of authentic knowledge amidst widespread deviation.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/134] Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. Masud from Ali b. al-Hasan b. Fadhal from al-Abbas b. Amir and Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Hukaym from Aban b. Uthman from al-Harith b. Mughira al-Nasri who said:

I heard Abd al-Malik b. A`yan asking Aba Abdillah عليه السلام – and he did not cease asking him – until he said to him: so the people were destroyed then (after the messenger of Allah)? he said: yes, by Allah, O the son of A`yan, all the people were destroyed, I (Abd al-Malik) said: whomever was in the east and the west? he said: it (the whole earth) was opened up to misguidance, yes, by Allah, they were all destroyed, except three, then joined Abu Sasan, Ammar, Shatira and Abu Umra, so they became seven.
